topic: Enterprise AI 2026: Agentic AI & Governance Trends

slides.title: Pilots flood into production
slides.body: Over half of enterprises plan to push a large share of AI experiments into live use within months. If your controls and training lag, you are scaling risk, not value.

slides.title: Agents outpace governance
slides.body: Autonomous and agentic systems are heading towards majority use, while most organisations still lack mature guardrails. When agents act across systems without clear policies, the audit trail fails.

slides.title: Efficiency hides a deeper miss
slides.body: Most teams chase quick productivity wins; far fewer are redesigning processes around AI. That gap is where competitors build new services while you keep polishing the old workflow.

slides.title: Roles stay static, work changes
slides.body: AI skill gaps remain the top blocker, and core roles are rarely rewritten for human–AI collaboration. If job design and KPIs stay pre‑AI, your people work around the tools, not with them.

slides.title: Sovereign AI becomes default
slides.body: Most enterprises now treat regional data control as non‑negotiable. That means traceable data flows and local vendors you can actually see into, not black‑box platforms you hope are compliant.

slides.title: Infrastructure ROI comes under audit
slides.body: Boards are starting to ask whether AI platforms, agents and SaaS spend tie to measurable outcomes. Without clean telemetry and clear success metrics, AI investment becomes an unprovable cost.

slides.title: What mature AI orgs do now
slides.body: They pair agentic AI builds with hard governance, redesign roles and processes around AI, and treat infrastructure visibility as a control. That is where we see faster deployment.

slides.line: Want your 2026 AI plan to survive scrutiny?

caption:
Agentic AI is arriving faster than your governance stack.

Most enterprises will push pilots into production while roles, policies and infrastructure visibility lag behind.
The result: more agents, same bottlenecks, higher risk.
